title: US, Swiss Authorities Unveil Major FIFA Corruption Cases
main_content:
Police in Switzerland arrested several senior officials from football’s governing body Wednesday in connection with a corruption indictment the U.S. Justice Department was expected to publicly announce later in the day.

The early morning arrests in Zurich came as FIFA officials gathered for meetings this week, including a session to elect the group’s president.

U.S. law enforcement officials said the indictment includes corruption charges against more than 10 FIFA officials and is the result of a multi-year investigation.

“The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of New York is investigating these individuals on suspicion of the acceptance of bribes and kickbacks between the early 1990s and the present day,” the Federal Office of Justice said in a statement.

FIFA President Sepp Blatter is not among those being charged. He is up for re-election to a fifth term on Friday.

The charges are the latest allegations of corruption involving FIFA under Blatter’s leadership. The bidding contests for both the 2018 and 2022 World Cup tournaments prompted an investigation by the group’s ethics committee, which concluded in November there were only “limited” ethics breaches and not sufficient evidence of bribery.

questions.question: Why were FIFA officials arrested?
options: They were caught stealing funds from the organization.
They were involved in a bribery scandal linked to World Cup bidding.
They were suspected of accepting bribes and kickbacks.
They were organizing illegal meetings in Zurich.
questions.answer: They were suspected of accepting bribes and kickbacks.

questions.question: How many officials are being charged?
During what period of time did the officials receive bribes and kickbacks?
options: From the late 1980s until the early 2000s.
Between the early 1990s and the present day.
questions.answer: Between the early 1990s and the present day.
